newsitem.title: MEXICO: Lawyer of jailed Mexican general held.
newsitem.headline: Lawyer of jailed Mexican general held.

text.p: Mexican police on Tuesday detained for questioning the lawyer of jailed Gen. Jesus Gutierrez Rebollo on accusations that he attempted to bribe witnesses, officials said.
The Mexican Attorney General's Office (PGR) also suggested in a statement that the lawyer may have helped in an armed attack on an informant last week.

Lawyer Tomas Arturo Gonzalez is one of four men defending Gutierrez Rebollo, the former head of the National Institute for Combating Drugs who was charged in February with being on the payroll of Mexico's most wanted drug trafficker.

Gonzalez was picked up at the maximum-security prison where Gutierrez Rebollo is held as the lawyer was on his way to attend a court hearing. Stunned family members of Gutierrez Rebollo immediately protested the move.

A PGR spokesman said police were complying with a prosecutor's order to have Gonzalez appear before authorities because he is a potential defendant. Gonzalez was released after a brief appearance, the spokesman said.
The PGR statement cited testimony from a witness who said Gonzalez had attempted to bribe former acquaintances of Gutierrez Rebollo in March to testify in the general's favour.

It also said that at least three people who had been "contacted and contracted" by Gonzalez in March took part in the shooting attack last Friday on informant Ricardo Cesareo Vazquez, who escaped unhurt. Cesareo Vazquez is a key witness against the general.
Authorities have sought to bolster their case against Gutierrez Rebollo, whose alleged misdeeds as head of the main anti-drug force damaged Mexico's law enforcement credibility.
This week, the military admitted that 34 other members of the armed forces had been arrested this year on drug charges.
